text: FIRST MOVE?

label: text
text: CHANG KAI-SHEK ON THE BOYCOTT

label: text
text: REPORT ED "FEELER."

label: text
text: " Alleged Opposition by the

label: text
text: The report is that General Cheung has caused inquiries to be made of the Strike Committee, as to what reception would be accorded if an order were made to call off the pickets. The boycott leaders are said to have indicated that there will be strenuous opposition to such a projected move.

label: text
text: Private Intelligence received from Canton indicates that General Cheung Kai-shek (the "soldier of the hour" in Kwang�ung) has put out a "feeler" towards ending the boycott of Hongkong.

label: text
text: A report on similar lines published by the "Kung Sheung" Yat Pei from their "Canton correspondent."

label: text
text: "The 'Wah Tze Yat Po" says that Mr. Eugene Chen's plan to restore (normal) communications between the two ports by temporary measures, until a settlement is arrived at, when the temporary measures will be reseinded.

label: paragraph_title
text: Official Communique.

label: text
text: The Canton Foreign Office has issued the following communiqué:

label: text
text: The Acting Minister for Foreign Affairs has written to the Governor of Hongkong, expressing the readiness of his Government to enter into negotiation with the Government of Hongkong regarding the Hongkong-Canton-Strike-and-intimating that his Government is prepared to appoint three Delegates with plenipotentiary powers. The suggestion is added that the Government of Hongkong would doubtless appoint the same number of Delegates with like powers to conduct the negotiation on its behalf.

label: paragraph_title
text: BEFORE JULY 30?

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cupton On Our “Suggested” Delegation.

label: text
text: Opponents to the plan for ending the—boycott—are—now—muttering charges that the Peasants, Labourers, Merchants and Educators Association is really a "meretool" in the hands of Chang Kaishek, and was organized by his henchmen in order to pass resolutions and bring pressure to end the boycott.

label: text
text: Optimists here predict that the boycott will be declared off before July 30. The plan now being formulated is to have three delegates from each city, the commissioners to have plenipotentiary powers. The Hongkong delegates for the final negotiations. (it will be suggested, so the report goes) shall be headed by an appointee of the Governor, and the other two shall represent the foreign, and the Chinese merchants of Hongkong. Canton's three delegates will represent the Government, the merchants of the city, and the strikers.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: PARADE TO BE HELD?

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.

label: text
text: Before Dr. C. C. Wu left for the North, it was the intention purposely to delay the concrete paying of the Shakee in order to make a dedication of that thoroughfare opposite Shameon impossible on June 23, the first anniversary of the shootings of last year.

label: text
text: Under the new regime, however, the paving is being rushed, and great preparations are being made for a dedication of the street and for re-naming it Avenue June 23. When Dr. Wu was Mayor it was felt that such a parade and dedication on June 23 would contain elements of danger, but now it is announced that the exercises will be held, and that absolute order and quiet will be maintained in order to refute the often-repeated charge that the Government cannot exert its authority even in the capital city.

label: paragraph_title
text: DOUGLAS CO.

label: text
text: ANNUAL MEETING.

label: text
text: Conditions adversely affecting the working of the Company were referred to at the annual meeting this morning of the Douglas Steamship Co., Ltd. but prospects of Brighter things ahead were held out.

label: text
text: Mr. H. P. White (Chairman of the Company) presided, supported by the Hon. Mr. D. G. M. Bernard, Mr. W. E. Clarke, the Hon. Mr. A. O. Lang and Mr. C. L. Farmer (Secretary).

label: text
text: The following shareholders were present: Messrs. Ho Leung, S. T. Williamson, A. H. White, E. Abraham and Chan Wing-kou.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chairman's Speech

label: text
text: The Chairman said: I very much regret to have to lay such an unsatisfactory statement before you, the loss on working being attributable to the conditions which arose as far back as last June.

label: text
text: The earnings of the steamers up to the beginning of that month were "fairly satisfactory", but the anti-British feeling and consequent Boycott in Canton added to the general unrest in China, effectually destroyed any prospect of profitable working.

label: text
text: The earnings of this company were particularly effected, as the ports at which its steamers usually call, were practically closed for the last six months of the year and only occasional and spasmodic sailings to the port of Foochow could be attempted by one or two of the steamers, the remainder being laid up during the half year. As far as the present year is concerned the situation is perhaps slightly better.

label: paragraph_title
text: Coastal Trade.

label: text
text: The port of Foochow has been working satisfactorily, and the company still controls a full share of the trade to and from that port, in spite of competition. Amoy reopened in April last, for the import and export of cargo and how is working normally. Swatow, however, remains entirely closed to all vessels sailing from Howick.

label: text
text: The "Hai-Foong" has been sold since the closing of the accounts, and we have been fortunate in obtaining charters for some of the steamers at rates which have enabled them to pay their way. All the steamers of the company are at present in commission.

label: text
text: There has been a great deal of sickness among the officers of the fleet, occasioning heavy expenditure for hospital and other expenses which is responsible for an increase of nearly $18,000 in charges under the heading—leave and pensions account.

label: text
text: Regarding the amount appearing in the accounts as due from the compradore, a large proportion has since been paid and we hold ample security for the remainder:

label: text
text: I do not think that there is anything more that can be added, but it is indeed difficult to forecast the future of shipping, for when the unfortunate tension that at present exists between Canton and Hongkong is relaxed, though the company retains the confidence of shippers, it must be borne in mind that there is a large number of steamers in this part of the world, and that competition at first, at any rate, may be expected to be very keen.

label: paragraph_title
text: Busines48.

label: text
text: I now beg to propose that the report and accounts as presented be adopted, and after this has been seconded will pleased to answer any questions to the best of my ability.

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. D. G. M. Bernard, Mr. W. E. Clarke and the Hon. Mr. A. O. Lang were elected as Consulting Committee for the ensuing year on the proposition of Mr. S. T. Williamson seconded by Mr. E. Abraham.

label: text
text: Mr. Ho Leung seconded and the report and accounts were unannously adopted.

label: text
text: Messrs. Lowe, Bingham and Matthews and Messrs. Linstend and Davis were appointed auditors for the ensuing year on the proposition of Mr. Chan Wing-kou, seconded by Mr. A. H. White, re-nuneration to be $500 each.

label: paragraph_title
text: AN “OLD HAND.”

label: paragraph_title
text: DEPARTURE OF CAPT. E.

label: text
text: PIRATE EXPERIENCES.

label: text
text: Leaving Hongkong to-morrow on the s.s. "Khyber" is one of the veteran river boat skippers very well-known in local shipping circles —Capt. Ebenezer Jones who, for over nine years has had charge of the s.s. "Ko Chow."

label: text
text: Capt. Jones's life in the East has not been without its thrilling experiences. In 1917, just after he had taken command of the "Ko Chow" he was pirated by the time old methods of "passengers" who had embarked disclosing themselves in their true capacity at a given signal.

label: text
text: In the defence of his vessel and its command, Capt. Jones was shot in the face, head and body and lost permanently the sight of one eye. The piracy occurred as the vessel was on its way from Doshing to Hongkong. As a recognition of his bravery the Government presented him with a cheque for £1,000.

label: text
text: More recently, about twelve months ago, Capt. Jones's vessel was among the three that were fired on when about a mile and a half in the buck reach on the Canton river—the shots being attributed to bandits which were particularly strong in the neighbourhood owing to disturbed conditions in Canton. The "Ko Chow" was put full steam ahead and ran the brunt of the fire whilst the other vessels have to. Little damage was done to the vessel.

label: text
text: Capt. Jones, whose "home is now" in Birkenhead, is of Welsh nationality and is a keen member of the Hongkong Gymdelthas Dewi Sant (St. David's Society). He has seldom been absent from any meeting or function held in connection with this organisation.

label: text
text: The good wishes of many friends will go with Capt. Jones in his well earned retirement.

label: paragraph_title
text: ROCKET SIGNALS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
PANIC AMONG VILLAGERS
AT UN LONG.

label: text
text: A FALSE ALARM

label: text
text: The peace of the police station at the outlying district of Au Tau in the New Territories was disturbed shortly after 1:30 this morning by several rockets which were observed above the village of Un Long in the distance.

label: text
text: This being an unusual occurrence, a message was immediately sent to police headquarters. This was followed by another message from Lokmachau police station on the other side where the rockets were also seen.

label: text
text: From inquiries made in official quarters this morning, it was gathered that later information from the New Territories showed that the alarm had been a false one. In addition to firearms kept for their own protection, the villagers of Un Long keep a quantity of rockets on hand to let off in case of an emergency such as an attack by robbers and warn the police stations. Apparently a villager heard a bang somewhere and let off a rocket, this being a signal to the other villagers to follow suit.

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICE DESERTER.

label: text
text: GETS JAIL WITHOUT THE OPTION.

label: text
text: HABIT TO BE STOPPED.

label: text
text: A. Shantung constable pleaded guilty at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning to a charge of deserting the force.

label: text
text: Mr. D. Burlingham prosecuting, said that the practice was becoming too common, as five constables had run away during last month. He asked for a heavy penalty — imprisonment without the option— in order to put a stop to this habit.

label: text
text: Defendant was sent to prison with hard labour for six months.

label: text
text: While several coolies were engaged in demolishing a house at Yu On Terrace yesterday, one of them accidentally fell from the scaffolding. He was picked up suffering from injuries to his head and shock and sent to the Government Civil Hospital.

label: paragraph_title
text: SMART CATCH.

label: text
text: PRISON AND BIRCH FOR SNATCHING

label: text
text: QUEEN'S ROAD INCIDENT.

label: paragraph_title
text: 一

label: text
text: Evidence was given by Mr. R. C. Mitchell, of the Sanitary Department, before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning in a case against a Chinese charged on remund with a snatching offence.

label: text
text: Witness said that while he was in his office at Beaconsfield Arcade on Tuesday last week he heard a commotion in the street during which police whistles were blown. On looking out he saw his office messenger chasing a Chinese (the defendant) in the direction of the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank where the man was stopped. Witness went to the place and saw a plain clothes constable also there. A search was carried out and the defendant had $19 in his pocket. Witness added that just then an elderly Chinese lady walked up to them and complained that the defendant snatched the money from her.

label: text
text: Defendant in a total denial of the offence said that he found the money on the ground, but he was identified by the complainant as the thief.

label: text
text: Sentence of six months' hard labour and 12 strokes of the birch was imposed

label: paragraph_title
text: CLUB'S TROUBLES.

label: text
text: "PAYING" MEMBER SUES ANOTHER.

label: text
text: "NOT AGAINST INDIVIDUAL."

label: text
text: When his club had been in financial difficulty, a Mr. Pun Pui-sheung had paid a certain sum which, he maintained, should have been paid by the members mutually; he claimed in the Summary Court for a refund to him, but judgment was given against him.

label: text
text: Mr. Justice J. R. Wood (Puisne Judge) ruled that in paying the cash, Mr. Pun (plaintiff) did so voluntarily, not acting under any obligation, nor as an authorised agent for the club. His status, therefore, (observed Mr. Wood) seemed to be that of an ordinary creditor of the club. As such, he may recover against the club but not against any individual member. His Lordship accordingly gave judgment for the defendant, with costs.

label: text
text:
In giving judgment, His Lordship said that plaintiff sued a fellow member to recover proportion of a sum of $857.94, paid by him for rent accrued, due in respect of club premises and other matters. Distress was levied by the landlord and in order to obtain release of the club's property, plaintiff paid the amounts claimed.
Mr. L. R. Andrewes (for Mr. Pun) asked for judgment to be reviewed. Mr. W. B. Hind-appeared for the fellow member.

label: paragraph_title
text: CATHOLIC BISHOP.

label: text
text: APOSTOLIC DELEGATE FOR CHINA ARRIVES.

label: text
text: CONSECRATION ON SUNDAY

label: text
text: His Grace the Archbishop C. Costantini the Apostolic Delegato for China arrived yesterday morning by the s.s. "President Cleveland."

label: text
text: His Grace will consécrate Bishop the Rt. Rev. H. Valtorta next Sunday at the Catholic Cathedral, the service will begin at 8:30 a.m. to which all Catholics are cordially invited.

label: text
text: The assistant prelates will be their Lordships José da Costa Nunes of Macao and A. Fourquet of Canton. The procession will be opened by the boy scouts, followed by the band of the Salesman Fathers of Macao, the clergy and the Bishops.

label: text
text: At 4 p.m. there will be a special thanksgiving service, after which, at the Mission House, the Catholic Community will be introduced to the new Bishop and to the Archbishop Delegate Tea will be served to visitors from 4:30 to 6 p.m. The Band of the Salesian Fathers will be in attendance.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON WINNING.

label: text
text:
VICTORIES IN HUNAN OVER
WU PEI-FU.

label: text
text: NORTHERN ROUT CLAIMED.

label: paragraph_title
text: General Chang And Soviet Principles

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton, June 9

label: text
text: To-day there is real jubilation in official circles in Canton over the receipt of delayed reports from General Tang Shang-chi, telling of important victories on four days over Wu Pei-fu's allies in Hunan.

label: text
text:
More than 2,000 rifles were captured, and two regiments of the "enemy's" troops were surrounded and disarmed. Large quantities of war supplies and food are also listed with the booty, and the Hunan troops of the enemy have given ground at several points and evacuated many important towns.
Generals Chung Tso-pei and Ho Chien co-operated in an attack at Yungfengtze, and drove the enemy to Chefutow. At Tsakiang the Hunanese also met severe reverses, and at the time of the last accounts, were giving ground rapidly in the sectors around Chitouwpu and Hsuanchow.

label: text
text: At Hunglomaio and Chinlantze the Hunanese were also defeated, and retreated to Siangsianghsien. The defeat of the armies from the North is described in official despatches as almost a rout, and Tang Shang-chí says that they will be pursued so rapidly that they will have no opportunity to re-organise.

label: paragraph_title
text: "Not So Cheerful."

label: text
text: From Kwangsi province the news is not so cheerful to the Cantonese, Nanning merchants have written to outside wholesalers asking them not to ship goods already ordered because they fear an immediate invasion by troops under General Tang Chi-yao, Pak Tai and other districts are already under martial law.

label: text
text: General Shen Hung-ying's forces have already taken possession of Chuen Chau, and General Han Tsol-fung has organised a force of 4,000 soldiers against Kwangtung and will join General Shen Hung-ying's armies in an effort to over-run the whole province. General Shen is being assisted by the counsel of one of Wu Pei-fu's able generals, Mr. Chai.

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek has issued a long statement in which he explains that he agreed to become commander-in-chief of the National Revolutionary Army only after repeated urging by the Central Kuomintang.

label: text
text: Soldiers Need Politics!

label: text
text: In his statement he deplores the fact that the Nationalist forces are really incompetent because they lack political training. He then announces that this political training will be his first care, and that "by following the training methods of the Soviet Revolutionary Army we hope to make our Kwangtung forces into a truly high-principled revolutionary army in order to realise National Revolution."

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek promises to uproot "long-standing corruption" from army circles, and ends by declaring that "now is the time and opportunity for us to overthrow the militarists of the North, to unify China, and convene a national conference."

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek yesterday inspected the 1st and 2nd regiments of the First Army, and the troops then started at once for the northern front.

label: text
text: Five more steamships have been sent to the southern district to bring 4,000 more of the troops of General Li Tsai-sum to Canton. When they arrive they will immediately entrain for Shiukwan and the northern front.

label: paragraph_title
text: WEATHER FORECAST.

label: text
text:
Until noon to-morrow, the forecast is variable winds, moderate; generally overcast, some rain.
To-day's Observatory report states that pressure has increased moderately from S. Manchuria to N. E. Japan. It has decreased moderately to slightly elsewhere. The two depressions have merged into one which is central over S. W. China and now dominates the map.
